points.description: Identifies that the background information (Mr. Leonard was a good athlete but not a good student, struggled with school work, lost his scholarship and flunked out because he couldn't read) made Paul relate to or empathise with him, since Paul recognised the same embarrassment and struggles from his own reading difficulties. Equivalent wording earns the mark.

Explains that this understanding changed Paul's attitude towards Mr. Leonard by making him want to help him in return, shown by Paul saying 'It's time to start your training' and offering to coach him. Accept any clear statement that Paul is motivated to repay or help Mr. Leonard, supported by a story detail.

rubric.notes: Full marks for explaining the effect of the background (Paul empathises with Mr. Leonard because of shared struggles with reading and school) and how this leads Paul to want to help him, with supporting detail from the story. One mark each for the empathy effect and for the resulting motivation to help; no partial credit as each idea is all-or-nothing.
